title: Primitive data types and their sizes

quiz.explain: int arithmetic overflows without an error and wraps to the smallest int.

options: Yes, but it prints a negative number
quiz.explain: Without L the literal is an int, and 48 billion does not fit in an int. Write 48000000000L.
72.5 is a double, which does not fit in a float without the f. D is fine: an int fits in a double.
The right side is calculated in int and overflows before it is stored in the long. 1000L * ... gives 31536000000.

quiz.q: How many bits does an int have?
quiz.explain: Java fixes the sizes on every platform: int is always 32 bits, long always 64.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a primitive type?
quiz.explain: String is a class (a reference type). The eight primitives are written in lower case.

options: No: possible lossy conversion from int to byte
quiz.explain: A byte holds -128 to 127. The compiler sees that 200 does not fit.

quiz.q: Which type is a whole-number literal like 42 without a suffix?
quiz.explain: Whole-number literals are int by default; decimal literals are double.

quiz.q: What changed for primitive types between Java 23 and Java 25?
options: Nothing in the sizes; primitive patterns are still a preview
quiz.explain: Sizes and ranges are unchanged since Java 1.0. Primitive types in patterns (instanceof int) are preview in 23 (JEP 455) and still preview in 25 (JEP 507).
